transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm mainly here because the clinic got on me about how little I've been eating. But most days, I mean, I'm just grabbing a coffee before my shift at the warehouse, and maybe a yogurt or a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... sitting down for an actual, real meal feels like it throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line.
When you think about eating more or gaining weight, what goes through your mind? Are you worried about how your body would look or feel?

I do worry about it, yeah. If I eat something heavier, like... I don't know, fried food from the break room at work, or a big plate at church, I get really scared it’s going to show on me right away. It just gets stuck in my head. I'll keep thinking about what I ate, and then I just want to go check the scale to see if it did.
After you eat something that worries you, do you do anything to try to get rid of it or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, exercising a lot, taking laxatives, or anything like that?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't mess with laxatives or anything like that. And honestly, I'm pretty worn out after packing boxes all day at the warehouse, so I don't really exercise either. I just... I mostly just stress about it and keep checking the scale.
Do you ever have times when you eat a lot of food in a short period of time—like feeling out of control with how much you're eating in one sitting?

No, not really. I don't ever eat a lot of food at once. It's kind of the opposite, honestly. Just... the idea of sitting down and eating a huge amount like that makes me too anxious. So, no, I don't ever have times where I lose control and just keep eating.
How much do you currently weigh, and has your weight dropped significantly over the past several months or year?

Right now, I weigh about 98 pounds. It's definitely gone down over the last year. I mean, my work pants are pretty loose on me now, and people at the warehouse have been telling me I look too thin. But honestly... when I see that number on the scale go down, it just feels like I'm finally getting somewhere. I just don't really see why everyone thinks I need to put the weight back on.
How tall are you, and over what period of time did your weight drop to 98 pounds?
I'm 5 foot 4. And... I guess the weight loss started about eight or nine months ago. It wasn't all at once, just kind of a steady drop since then.
At your lowest weight during this past year, how much did you weigh?
This is it, actually. 98 pounds is the lowest I've been. It's just been going down steadily, so... yeah, I haven't weighed any less than what I do right now.
At 5 foot 4 and 98 pounds, have you noticed any physical changes like feeling cold all the time, your period stopping, or feeling dizzy or weak?

Um... honestly, I haven't really noticed any of that. I don't feel dizzy or weak at work, and I'm on my feet all day. As for feeling cold or my period... I mean, nothing that really stands out to me. I feel fine, mostly.

At 5 foot 4 inches and 98 pounds, do you know what your BMI is, or would you like me to calculate it for you? I ask because there are specific weight ranges that help us understand the severity of what's going on.

I don't know my BMI. You can calculate it if you want. I know you and the people from my church are worried about my weight, but I honestly think everyone is making a bigger deal out of it than it really is. I'm still going to work every day, doing my classes, and keeping up with everything in my life just fine.

Your BMI is approximately 16.8, which is considered significantly below the healthy range. Given that you're at this weight and have lost it steadily over eight or nine months, do you understand why doctors and your family are concerned about your health, or does it still feel like they're overreacting?

I mean... I hear what you're saying about the number being low. But yeah, it still feels like an overreaction to me. 

Like I was just saying, I get why you and the folks at church are looking at the weight and getting worried, but... I just think everyone is blowing it out of proportion. If things were really as bad as you're making it sound, I wouldn't be able to stand on my feet packing boxes at work all day, or get my classes done. I'm keeping up with my life completely fine, so... I just don't see why it's such a huge deal.
